source.title: Wiring Beats Blending: Structure-Aware Compensation for Transformer Downscaling

record.file_problem: The paper text is complete and readable. Some PDF table and equation formatting is flattened, but the alignment results are identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-size representation alignment using held-out ridge R2, Procrustes R2, and linear CKA. These are different measures from the broad convergence claim and test whether representations align, but the study does not test a scaling trend across multiple sizes.
record.gate_note: The alignment experiment is for one Pythia pair, 1.4B→410M, using shared inputs. It reports representation measurements and linear-map results. The reported embedding-weight R2 values (0.248 input, 0.386 output) concern parameters rather than representations and are not rows. The paper does not measure alignment across a scale sweep, cross-modal pairs, or independent training seeds.
record.test_reason: Section 4 and Appendix A.2 measure held-out linear and Procrustes maps and linear CKA between Pythia-1.4B and Pythia-410M activations on shared Pile inputs. This bears directly on V4 (linear interchangeability) and, through the measure and estimator comparisons, on V6. It is a different method from the originals' mutual-kNN/scale sweep, used as a diagnostic inside a downscaling paper. Only one same-family pair with identical data and tokenizer is analysed.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Within the Pythia family (identical data and tokenizer), activations align strongly across sizes under a linear map (held-out ridge R2 0.84, mostly a change of basis per Procrustes 0.717), while raw parameters align weakly. CKA is used only descriptively because it saturates and gives coarse layer correspondence. The paper's main conclusions concern downscaling conversion (structure-preserving selection, compensation and rescale) rather than representation convergence itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a single within-family size pair, held-out activation mapping, Procrustes, and CKA calibration; it does not test a broad cross-architecture or cross-modal scaling trend.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported alignment magnitude varies across ridge R2, Procrustes R2, and linear CKA. CKA's biased and debiased estimates match in the reported calibration; its same-index best-match fraction is also unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameters align weakly across sizes even where representations align. Embedding-matrix ridge R2 is 0.248 (input) and 0.386 (output) vs 0.844 for activations. A target-peeking shared operator explains at most ~30% of weight variance, and post-operator weight residuals carry no learnable or transferable signal (p≥0.99).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational convergence across model sizes does not imply parameter-level correspondence; weights of same-family models are only weakly linearly related.

record.problems: The representation comparison covers one size pair in one model family, whose members share training data and tokenizer. It does not test a scale trend, capability dependence, cross-modal alignment, or out-of-distribution robustness. The paper notes that CKA's middle layers saturate and uses it descriptively.
record.rows_left_out: Parameter-alignment measurements (embedding weight R2 values) are omitted because they measure stored weights rather than representations or distances between inputs. Other conversion and training results do not measure the claim's representation-alignment object.

untested.parts: No trend across sizes or capability; only one representation pair (1.4B→410M) is analysed. The 6.9B and Qwen3 pairs get no alignment measurement.
No models differing only in seed; seeds here are data-draw seeds for continued training.
Untested: stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, and cross-architecture or cross-data pairs.
No shared interpretable features or circuits.
Untested: neighbour counts, input distribution, and out-of-distribution inputs. Only measure type and CKA estimator/sample size vary.
Untested: whether alignment plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives explain it. The pair shares data, tokenizer and architecture by design.

missing.what: Per-layer held-out R2 profile: ridge and Procrustes dip together at layers 3–5, the layers CKA also flags as distinct
Off-diagonal and all-pairs CKA means (trained 0.695/0.704 vs untrained 0.056/0.054) and untrained best-on-diagonal 0.042, needed as baselines

record.verdict_notes: Representation alignment is a diagnostic section in a model-conversion paper. All alignment evidence comes from one same-family, same-data pair, so it cannot separate a common world model from shared training data (V7). The untrained-model CKA rows are controls and should serve as baselines rather than standalone results. Rows r4/r5 originally carried inconsistent states; their meaning here is that the estimator change had no effect.

versions.untested_parts: No trend in alignment across multiple model sizes or capability levels is measured; only one pair of sizes is analyzed.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions are studied.
No comparison across training initializations or shared feature subspaces across seeds is reported.
Tests held-out linear maps on pooled activations for one Pythia size pair; it does not test layer stitching, relative representations, or mappings without paired inputs.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.

Compares several similarity measures and CKA estimator settings on the same family and frozen inputs. It does not systematically vary input distributions, neighbor counts, or out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not compare training data or objectives to determine why alignment occurs, or test whether alignment plateaus. Its pair shares data and tokenizer.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B vs. Pythia-410M
rows.stage_stated: pretrained models; exact stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fit a per-layer large-to-small ridge linear map on pooled activations and evaluate held-out R2.
rows.note: The authors describe the smaller model's pooled representation as largely a linear projection of the larger model's.
rows.check: For V4, held-out ridge R2 0.844 shows a near-full linear map. For V6 it is one of three measures compared and should be read with r2/r3. No baseline is given; the paper gives no random-model R2.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4; Appendix A.2; Table 7, pooled activations row.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B vs. Pythia-410M
rows.stage_stated: pretrained models; exact stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fit a per-layer Procrustes map, using rotation plus one global scale, on pooled activations and evaluate held-out R2.
rows.note: This is lower than the full linear ridge result; the authors characterize the difference as non-orthogonal reshaping.
rows.check: Rotation-plus-scale gives 0.717, clearly below ridge (0.844). An orthogonal map leaves ~28% unexplained, so partial for 'little loss' under the simplest map.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B vs. Pythia-410M
rows.stage_stated: pretrained models; exact stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compute linear CKA between corresponding layers' pooled activations.
rows.note: The paper says CKA shows a saturated middle band and uses held-out R2, rather than CKA, as its decisive alignment measure.
rows.check: CKA 0.883 is close to the map-based values, so alignment does not vanish under this measure. The paper says the middle band saturates (~1.0), so the magnitude is only coarsely informative. Baseline should be the untrained-model floor (0.059, Table 6).

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B vs. Pythia-410M
rows.stage_stated: pretrained models; exact stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measure how often a layer's best CKA match is its same-index layer.

conditions.value: 16k tokens per layer from the similarity subset

rows.measure: Fraction of 1.4B layers whose best-matching 410M layer has the same index
rows.note: The paper describes the CKA correspondence as coarse; this fraction is unchanged under debiasing.
rows.check: Only 12.5% same-index best matches (vs 4.2% for the untrained control, Table 6, not recorded as baseline). CKA resolves only coarse early/mid/late correspondence despite a high diagonal mean. This is a measure-resolution limit rather than alignment vanishing.

statements.correction: Pythia-1.4B versus 410M: diagonal CKA = 0.898 for both estimators on 16k tokens; biased CKA = 0.883 on 64k tokens; estimator bias described as negligible; no calibrated alignment-versus-size sweep reported.
statements.problem: The equal biased/debiased CKA values are supported. Any attribution of persistent layer-max size trends or fixed-depth calibrated trends to this study is unsupported; its alignment analysis uses one size pair.
